Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 1) Permanent cessation of circulation, respiration and brain function is called:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Somatic death means death of the body as a whole. It involves permanent cessation of circulation, respiration and brain function.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 2) Irreversible cessation of all brain and brainstem functions is:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Brain death means irreversible loss of all brain and brainstem functions. It is considered legal death.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 3) Death trance is also known as:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Death trance is a state where signs of life are greatly reduced, so the person appears dead though life is still present.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 4) In the tripod of life, the three vital systems are brain, heart and:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: The tripod of life includes brain, heart and lungs. Failure of these systems produces coma, syncope and asphyxia.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 5) Mode of death due to brain failure is:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Coma is the mode of death due to failure of brain function. It is one of the three classical modes of death.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 6) Mode of death due to heart failure is:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Syncope is the mode of death due to heart failure. It represents failure of circulation.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 7) Mode of death due to respiratory failure is:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Asphyxia is the mode of death due to respiratory failure. It results from failure of oxygenation.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 8) Immediate postmortem change includes stoppage of:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Immediate changes after death are stoppage of brain function, respiration and circulation. These represent failure of vital systems.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 9) Pallor after death is classified as:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Pallor mortis is an early postmortem change. It occurs due to cessation of circulation.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 10) Cooling of body after death is called:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Algor mortis means cooling of the body after death. It is an early postmortem change.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 11) Postmortem hypostasis is also known as:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Livor mortis means postmortem staining or hypostasis. It occurs due to settling of blood in dependent parts.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 12) Stiffening of muscles after death is called:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Rigor mortis is postmortem stiffening of muscles. It is an early postmortem change.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 13) Putrefaction is classified as:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Putrefaction is a late postmortem change. It represents decomposition of the body after death.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 14) Adipocere formation is classified as:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Adipocere formation is a late postmortem change. It occurs after decomposition of body fat under suitable conditions.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 15) Mummification is classified as:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Mummification is a late postmortem change. It occurs due to drying and preservation of the body.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 16) The surest sign of death is:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Putrefaction is the surest sign of death. It indicates definite decomposition after death.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 17) A late sign of death is:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Adipocere formation is a late postmortem change. Cooling and rigor occur earlier after death.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 18) Pallor mortis usually appears within:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Pallor mortis appears within 0–2 hours after death. It is among the earliest visible postmortem changes.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 19) Livor mortis usually begins at:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Livor mortis begins around 1–2 hours after death. It later becomes fixed.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 20) Rigor mortis usually begins at:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Rigor mortis begins around 1–2 hours after death. It becomes complete later.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 21) Rigor mortis usually becomes complete at:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Rigor mortis usually becomes complete within 6–12 hours after death. It then persists before disappearing.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 22) Lividity usually becomes fixed at:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Lividity becomes fixed at around 12 hours after death. Fixed lividity helps assess postmortem body position.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 23) Rigor mortis usually disappears at:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Rigor mortis usually disappears within 18–36 hours. Its disappearance is related to decomposition.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 24) Putrefaction usually begins at:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Putrefaction usually begins within 24–48 hours. The early green discoloration appears over the right iliac fossa.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 25) Early green discoloration of putrefaction usually appears over:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Putrefaction commonly begins as green discoloration over the right iliac fossa. This is due to intestinal bacterial activity.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 26) Rigor mortis and algor mortis are useful for estimating:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Rigor mortis and algor mortis are useful indicators for estimating time since death. Environmental factors must also be considered.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 27) Livor mortis is useful for assessing:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Livor mortis forms in dependent parts of the body. Its distribution helps assess body position after death.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 28) Fixed lividity mainly indicates:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Fixed lividity reflects the position in which blood settled after death. It can help detect postmortem movement of the body.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 29) Absence of rigor mortis is associated with death due to:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: The file notes no rigor mortis in death due to septicemia. Severe infection may alter normal postmortem muscle changes.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 30) Rigor mortis appears early but disappears late in:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Strychnine poisoning is associated with early appearance and late disappearance of rigor mortis. It is related to intense muscular activity.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 31) Rigor mortis appears early but disappears late in:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Spinal poisoning is listed with early appearance and late disappearance of rigor mortis. It is an important special association.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 32) Hyoid bone fracture is associated with:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Hyoid bone fracture may be found in hanging. Neck structures must be examined carefully in asphyxial deaths.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 33) Ligature mark is especially associated with:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Ligature mark is an important autopsy finding in strangulation or throttling. Its direction and level help differentiate from hanging.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 34) Pugilistic attitude is associated with:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Pugilistic attitude is seen in burns. It occurs due to heat-induced contraction of muscles.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 35) Defensive wounds suggest:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Defensive wounds indicate an attempt to protect oneself from assault. They strongly suggest homicidal violence.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 36) Cyanosis is associated with:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Cyanosis is associated with asphyxia due to reduced oxygenation. It may be seen in mechanical asphyxial deaths.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 37) The usual manner of death in hanging is:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Hanging is usually suicidal. The ligature mark is typically oblique and non-continuous.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 38) The usual manner of death in strangulation is:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Strangulation is usually homicidal. It commonly shows a horizontal continuous ligature mark with congested face.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 39) Ligature mark in typical hanging is:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: In typical hanging, the ligature mark is oblique. It usually runs upward toward the point of suspension.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 40) Ligature mark in hanging is usually:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: In hanging, the ligature mark is usually non-continuous. It is often incomplete near the knot area.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 41) Ligature mark in hanging is usually situated:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: In hanging, the ligature mark is usually above the thyroid cartilage. It is classically oblique and non-continuous.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 42) Ligature mark in strangulation is usually:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: In strangulation, the ligature mark is usually horizontal. It commonly encircles the neck.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 43) Ligature mark in strangulation is usually:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Strangulation usually produces a continuous ligature mark. It may completely encircle the neck.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 44) Ligature mark in strangulation is commonly situated:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: In strangulation, the ligature mark is usually horizontal, continuous and at or below the thyroid cartilage.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 45) Face in hanging is commonly:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: The face in hanging is usually pale. Venous obstruction is less marked than in strangulation.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 46) Face in strangulation is commonly:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: In strangulation, the face is commonly congested and cyanosed. This occurs due to venous obstruction and asphyxia.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 47) Characteristic finding in hanging is:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Dribbling of saliva from the angle of the mouth is characteristic of hanging. It supports antemortem suspension.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 48) Salivary dribbling in strangulation is usually:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Salivary dribbling is characteristic of hanging. It is usually absent in strangulation.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 49) Hyoid bone fracture in hanging:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Hyoid bone fracture may occur in hanging. It depends on age, force and neck structures.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 50) Hyoid bone fracture in strangulation is described as:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: The document describes hyoid bone fracture as uncommon in strangulation. Other signs must be assessed together.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 51) Thyroid cartilage fracture is more common in:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Thyroid cartilage fracture is more common in strangulation. Direct neck compression is stronger than in typical hanging.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 52) Thyroid cartilage fracture is less common in:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: In hanging, thyroid cartilage fracture is less common. Strangulation produces greater direct compression of the neck.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 53) Completely encircling ligature mark suggests:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: A completely encircling and continuous ligature mark is more suggestive of strangulation. Hanging usually produces an incomplete mark.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 54) Transverse ligature mark over neck suggests:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: A transverse or horizontal ligature mark is typical of strangulation. Hanging usually produces an oblique mark.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 55) Oblique, non-continuous ligature mark above thyroid cartilage indicates:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Hanging classically shows an oblique, non-continuous ligature mark above thyroid cartilage. Salivary dribbling may also be present.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 56) Horizontal, continuous ligature mark at or below thyroid cartilage indicates:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Strangulation classically shows a horizontal, continuous ligature mark at or below thyroid cartilage. The face is often congested.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 57) Pale face with salivary dribbling favours:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Hanging commonly shows pale face with salivary dribbling. These findings help differentiate it from strangulation.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 58) Congested cyanosed face with absent salivary dribbling favours:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Strangulation commonly shows congested, cyanosed face and absence of salivary dribbling. Ligature mark is usually horizontal and continuous.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 59) Body position after death is best assessed by:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Livor mortis forms in dependent areas. Its distribution helps determine the position of the body after death.

Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.question: 60) Time since death is better estimated by:
Post mortem changes, Hanging , time sinc.exp: Rigor mortis and algor mortis are useful for estimating time since death. Livor mortis is more useful for body position.
